head: 44f4bc6321ff3fa1eeca3ed688b71f2feff31d36
claim: A byokit release publish now skips a package name the npm registry has never had, names each skip in the run summary, and still publishes the existing packages; any other publish failure still fails the run.

target.version: byokit release tooling (scripts/release.ts) at this commit

steps.start: main at 36359ffe: @byokit/herdr 0.19.0 pending, six never-published names (share, outbox, pi, approve, service, speak) also pending, one failed name failed the whole publish
steps: Run the release tests against a fake registry: a refused publish of a name that exists exits 1 and names the failure; a never-published name is skipped and named; an all-skipped run exits 0 and says nothing was published
Run `release publish --dry-run` on the current tree with real registry reads
steps.result: The dry run skips exactly share, outbox, pi, approve, service and speak with one line each and publishes @byokit/herdr@0.19.0; the tests show a failed existing name still exits non-zero

verdicts.seen: Read the capture (test lines plus dry-run output). Tests: 'publish skips a never-published name, names it, and still fails a refused existing name' and 'publish exits clean when the only pending names are skipped, naming each', pass 11, fail 0, exit 0. Dry-run lists six lines like 'skipped @byokit/share@0.1.1: name never published to npm (registry read answers E404)', each naming the skip, then 'published this run: @byokit/herdr@0.19.0', exit 0. This shows skipping never-published names, naming each in the summary, and still publishing the existing package. The 'other failures still fail' part is covered by the test refusing an existing name (exit 1). No contradiction.
